question.text: When computing free-float market capitalisation for a value-weighted index like the Nifty 50 or BSE Sensex (used by Aravalli Long-Short Fund as a hedge benchmark), which ONE of the following categories of shareholding is INCLUDED in free float (i.e., NOT excluded)?

answer.text: Shares held by founders / directors / acquirers with control element
Shares held by the Government as promoter / acquirer
Non-strategic / public free-float holdings that fall outside the workbook's exclusion list
Locked-in shares that cannot be sold in the open market in normal course

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Box 8.2 ('Concept of Free Float'), free float EXCLUDES: control/promoter holdings, government promoter/acquirer stakes, FDI-route holdings, strategic stakes, associate/cross-holdings, employee welfare trusts, and locked-in shares. Free float is, by elimination, the residual non-strategic / public holding that does not fall within any of those exclusion buckets. The Trap: Options A, B, and D are all directly named on the workbook's exclusion list. Only Option C — the residual public/non-strategic holding — is genuinely floating and therefore counted in free-float market capitalisation. Note: The workbook defines free float by listing what is excluded; anything outside those exclusions counts as free float.
